meta.updateStatus: Curated evidence reviewed; no deterministic updater
meta.scope: Bounded tasks in transport, medicine, language, media, vision, and logistics

question: When does AI become fast enough, reliable enough, and authorized enough to close a real-world loop?

verdict.label: Conditional
verdict.text: AI already closes selected bounded loops before their environments change, but timing success and benchmark accuracy do not establish field reliability, authority, scale, safety, or position removal.
verdict.short: Some bounded loops close. Few justify broad autonomy claims.

loopStages.label: Sense
loopStages.question: Capture task-relevant state before it expires.

loopStages.label: Interpret
loopStages.question: Convert signals into a usable representation.

loopStages.label: Predict
loopStages.question: Estimate state, outcome, or next event.

loopStages.label: Decide
loopStages.question: Select an action inside explicit constraints.

loopStages.label: Act
loopStages.question: Change the task environment or route work.

loopStages.label: Observe
loopStages.question: Detect result, failure, or need for fallback.

timingClasses.label: Hard real time
timingClasses.definition: Missing a specified deadline constitutes system failure.

timingClasses.label: Operational real time
timingClasses.definition: Response must arrive inside a process-control window; occasional misses require containment.

timingClasses.label: Interactive real time
timingClasses.definition: Response cadence must preserve a usable human interaction.

timingClasses.label: Near real time
timingClasses.definition: Result must arrive during the encounter, shift, or decision window.

timingClasses.label: Offline intelligence
timingClasses.definition: Useful output can arrive after the environment or workflow has paused.

maturityStates.label: Demonstrated
maturityStates.question: Has the bounded loop worked under documented conditions?

maturityStates.label: Operational
maturityStates.question: Is it used in a real workflow rather than only a benchmark or lab?

maturityStates.label: Reliable
maturityStates.question: Does field evidence support performance across intended conditions and failures?

maturityStates.label: Approved
maturityStates.question: Does a relevant authority permit this intended use, or is approval not applicable?

maturityStates.label: Scaled
maturityStates.question: Is sustained use documented across material volume or sites?

cases.label: Geofenced autonomous driving
cases.boundary: Dynamic driving task inside a permit-defined operational design domain; not unrestricted driving.
cases.geographyPopulation: California public roads; permitted manufacturers and vehicles
cases.period: California permit status reviewed through August 2026; federal crash-reporting framework amended through 2025
cases.deadline: Vehicle-control cycle before road state invalidates the action; exact deadline is system-specific
cases.intendedUse: Navigate, control speed, and respond to road users within approved location, weather, speed, and operating constraints
cases.unitDenominator: Permit categories and reportable incidents; NHTSA reports are not normalized by miles, fleet size, or ODD exposure
cases.interpretation: Public-road operation demonstrates a bounded closed loop and regulatory authorization in named domains.
cases.caveat: Permits are not proof of comparative safety. Raw report counts are not incident counts or comparative safety rates; reports can be duplicated and lack exposure denominators.
cases.humanFallback: Remote assistance, minimal-risk stop, passenger or fleet support, and emergency services; exact design is operator-specific.
cases.failureBoundary: Outside approved geography, weather, speed, road type, sensor visibility, or system capability; rare interactions and incident recovery.

cases.label: Autonomous retinal screening
cases.boundary: Detect more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy from specified retinal images in eligible adults with diabetes; not treatment or a general eye examination.
cases.geographyPopulation: United States; indicated primary-care patients with diabetes and no prior diabetic retinopathy diagnosis
cases.period: FDA De Novo decision 11 April 2018; pivotal trial published 2018; Johns Hopkins deployment comparison 2019–2021
cases.deadline: Near-real-time result during a primary-care encounter; acquisition and quality retries remain part of workflow
cases.intendedUse: Return an autonomous screening result or image-quality failure and route indicated patients to eye care
cases.unitDenominator: 900 enrolled pivotal-trial participants; deployment study included more than 17,000 adult patients with diabetes
cases.interpretation: A narrow medical loop has authorization, prospective diagnostic validation, and documented health-system operation.
cases.caveat: Authorization and diagnostic accuracy do not prove completed referral, treatment, long-run outcomes, generalization, or scale.
cases.humanFallback: Repeat image acquisition, clinician review, referral to an eye-care professional, and usual care when no result is returned.
cases.failureBoundary: Ineligible patient, inadequate image quality, disease outside intended use, missed disease, false referral, or failed downstream follow-up.

cases.label: Interactive LLM response
cases.boundary: Generate and stream text for a submitted prompt; not verify truth, complete external work, or own consequences.
cases.geographyPopulation: Benchmark systems and datasets; not a population estimate
cases.period: MLPerf Inference v6.0 results published April 2026
cases.deadline: Interactive benchmark constrains time to first token and time per output token; application tolerance varies
cases.intendedUse: Preserve conversational response cadence under benchmarked server load
cases.unitDenominator: Queries and generated tokens under MLPerf workload, model, accuracy, latency, and submission rules
cases.interpretation: Latency-constrained generation is measurable jointly with benchmark quality requirements.
cases.caveat: A compliant benchmark run does not establish factuality, field reliability, task completion, approval, or product-wide service quality.
cases.humanFallback: User correction, source inspection, retry, tool confirmation, or escalation to a responsible person.
cases.failureBoundary: Unsupported request, hallucination, unsafe output, excessive latency, context loss, tool failure, or unobserved downstream effect.

cases.label: Streaming image generation
cases.boundary: Continuously update generated imagery from changing input on specified GPU pipelines; not general visual truth or production reliability.
cases.geographyPopulation: Research hardware and benchmark inputs; not a human population
cases.deadline: Frame or update cadence fast enough for documented interactive generation on tested hardware
cases.intendedUse: Provide continuous visual feedback while a user changes prompts or input streams
cases.unitDenominator: Frames or images per unit time on reported model, pipeline, resolution, and hardware
cases.interpretation: Pipeline-level research demonstrates hardware-specific interactive diffusion generation.
cases.caveat: Demo throughput does not establish stable quality, safety, rights clearance, operational service, or scale.
cases.humanFallback: Pause, regenerate, edit manually, reject output, or switch to offline rendering.
cases.failureBoundary: Hardware mismatch, quality collapse, temporal inconsistency, unsafe content, prompt drift, or missed interaction cadence.

cases.label: Real-time object identification
cases.boundary: Classify or detect objects from benchmark-defined images; not open-world scene understanding.
cases.geographyPopulation: ImageNet-2012 and OpenImages benchmark samples; not geographic or population inference
cases.deadline: Model- and scenario-specific latency constraint; ResNet50 server scenario specifies 15 ms
cases.intendedUse: Measure image classification or object detection throughput and latency while meeting stated accuracy targets
cases.unitDenominator: Benchmark queries on fixed validation datasets, quality targets, load scenarios, hardware, and software
cases.interpretation: A benchmark can demonstrate latency plus accuracy for a fixed task and dataset.
cases.caveat: Fixed-dataset accuracy does not prove field reliability under distribution shift, occlusion, novel classes, or sensor failure.
cases.humanFallback: Reject low-confidence output, stop downstream actuation, request another view, or send to human review.
cases.failureBoundary: Open-set object, domain shift, poor lighting, occlusion, adversarial input, sensor fault, or deadline miss.

cases.label: Warehouse sorting
cases.boundary: Pick and singulate packages from unstructured piles in a named robotic induction fleet; adjacent transport, packing, maintenance, and exceptions remain separate.
cases.geographyPopulation: Amazon Robotics production facilities and handled packages; locations not enumerated in source
cases.period: Deployment evidence reported at IROS workshop in 2023
cases.deadline: Operational cycle must keep pace with induction flow; source reports daily fleet volume rather than per-item deadline
cases.intendedUse: Select feasible picks, manipulate packages, and route failed attempts within robotic induction
cases.unitDenominator: Vendor-authored extended abstract reports fleet handling up to 6 million packages per day and more than 2 billion cumulative manipulations
cases.interpretation: Vendor research documents scaled production use of learned pick-success estimation in one bounded warehouse loop.
cases.caveat: Vendor-authored aggregate volume lacks independent reliability, exception-rate, economics, worker-outcome, and site-level denominators.
cases.humanFallback: Operators handle damaged, unsafe, ungraspable, misrouted, or repeatedly failed packages and maintain equipment.
cases.failureBoundary: Deformable or unknown package, clutter, bad grasp, damage risk, congestion, hardware fault, or downstream routing exception.

distribution.label: Automatable loop
distribution.text: Only stages inside the stated task boundary; adjacent work is not silently absorbed.

distribution.label: Possible position effects
distribution.text: Demand, workflow redesign, economics, authority, and exception load mediate any staffing effect.

distribution.label: Retained human work
distribution.text: Goal setting, context, consent, physical preparation, verification, care, maintenance, and accountability.

distribution.label: Exception handling
distribution.text: Out-of-domain cases, low confidence, unsafe states, damaged inputs, appeals, and recovery.

distribution.label: Affected groups
distribution.text: Operators, patients, road users, customers, workers, bystanders, reviewers, and people represented in data.

competingExplanations.label: Constrained environment
competingExplanations.text: Geofencing, fixed routes, controlled lighting, known objects, or narrow intended use can close a loop without general intelligence.

competingExplanations.label: Hardware
competingExplanations.text: Accelerators, robotics, networks, and control systems may create the timing gain.

competingExplanations.label: Sensors
competingExplanations.text: Better cameras, calibration, redundancy, and input quality may dominate model changes.

competingExplanations.label: Human fallback
competingExplanations.text: People may absorb rare cases, recovery, quality control, or responsibility outside headline automation.

competingExplanations.label: Integration
competingExplanations.text: Workflow redesign, data plumbing, interfaces, and maintenance can determine operational performance.

competingExplanations.label: Regulation
competingExplanations.text: Permits and intended-use controls can both enable and bound real deployment.

competingExplanations.label: Model gains
competingExplanations.text: Accuracy, latency, planning, or generation improvements matter only after competing system changes are separated.

upgrade: Repeated field evidence reports denominator-aware deadline misses, failures, interventions, and recovery.
Independent evaluation covers intended populations, operating domains, distribution shift, and rare conditions.
Authority, integration, economics, and exception handling remain effective across sustained volume.
Observed downstream outcomes improve without shifting hidden cost or risk to another group.
downgrade: A permit, benchmark, or demo is generalized beyond its stated operating domain.
Latency improves while task accuracy, safety, or downstream outcome worsens.
Human intervention, exception work, or exposure denominators disappear from reporting.
New conditions produce correlated failures, unsafe actions, or responsibility gaps.

feedbackRisks.label: Latency
feedbackRisks.text: A late safe answer can become an unsafe action in a moving environment.

feedbackRisks.label: Distribution shift
feedbackRisks.text: The next input may leave the benchmark or intended-use distribution.

feedbackRisks.label: Surveillance
feedbackRisks.text: Closing observation loops can expand collection about workers, patients, bystanders, and places.

feedbackRisks.label: Cyberattack
feedbackRisks.text: Sensors, models, interfaces, and actuators add attack surfaces.

feedbackRisks.label: Cascading actions
feedbackRisks.text: Fast coupled systems can propagate one error before human review.

feedbackRisks.label: Responsibility gaps
feedbackRisks.text: Operator, deployer, vendor, and authority roles can diverge at failure time.

feedbackRisks.label: Deskilling
feedbackRisks.text: Long-run reliance can weaken fallback capability even when fallback remains formally required.

feedbackRisks.label: Rebound demand
feedbackRisks.text: Cheaper or faster decisions can increase total actions, energy use, monitoring, or exception volume.

possibilities.text: Smaller, local models may close more useful loops by reducing network latency and data transfer, even when benchmark capability trails larger systems.
Exception-handling quality may become a stronger operational bottleneck than model inference speed.
Organizations may redesign jobs around supervising several bounded loops rather than removing whole positions.
Which actions should remain slow enough for contestability, consent, or human judgment?
Who should bear proof and liability when a system acts before affected people can intervene?

method.loopRule: Evaluate a bounded task only when Sense → Interpret → Predict → Decide → Act → Observe closes before the task environment changes enough to invalidate the action.
method.maturityRule: Benchmark accuracy does not prove field reliability; authorization does not prove scale; scale does not prove safety.
method.unknownRule: Unknown is not failed. Approval may be not applicable where no task-specific authorization regime applies.
method.positionRemovalRule: Position-removal claims require full-loop coverage plus reliable operation, authority, integration, economics, and exception handling. Otherwise describe task change, exposure, or augmentation.
method.refresh: Monthly editorial replay of source dates, intended uses, permit or authorization scope, field evidence, and caveats. No visitor-time evidence calls.

sources.title: Autonomous Vehicle Permit Holders
sources.date: Testing-with-driver list as of August 12, 2026; driverless list updated April 3, 2026; deployment list as of November 21, 2025
sources.geographyPopulation: California public roads; named AV manufacturers and permit categories
sources.deadline: Permit page specifies location, time, weather, and speed boundaries rather than control-cycle deadlines
sources.intendedUse: Testing with driver, driverless testing, and deployment under category-specific conditions
sources.denominatorUnit: Permit holders and approved operating conditions; not safety rates
sources.role: Establishes bounded public-road authorization and operational design domains
sources.interpretation: Some autonomous driving is authorized inside explicit operating constraints.
sources.caveat: Permit status does not establish comparative safety, reliability, fleet scale, or unrestricted autonomy.

sources.institution: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
sources.title: Standing General Order on Crash Reporting
sources.geographyPopulation: Named US ADS and Level 2 ADAS manufacturers and operators; reportable public-road crashes
sources.deadline: Crash reporting concerns systems used within 30 seconds before covered crashes; not control latency
sources.intendedUse: Timely safety oversight and potential defect investigation
sources.denominatorUnit: Submitted crash reports; possible duplicate reports and no common mileage, fleet, or ODD exposure denominator
sources.role: Defines incident-reporting scope and interpretation limits
sources.interpretation: Incident files can identify events and safety concerns.
sources.caveat: Raw report counts are not incident counts or comparative safety rates.

sources.title: De Novo Classification Request for IDx-DR, DEN180001
sources.geographyPopulation: United States; indicated adults with diabetes in primary-care settings
sources.period: Premarket evidence reviewed for 2018 De Novo decision
sources.deadline: Encounter-scale autonomous result; device summary does not define a universal real-time class
sources.intendedUse: Autonomous detection of more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy under labeled conditions
sources.denominatorUnit: Device-level benefit-risk and clinical performance evidence under intended use
sources.role: Establishes authorization, intended use, controls, and failure boundaries
sources.interpretation: FDA classified the bounded retinal diagnostic software as Class II.
sources.caveat: Marketing authorization is not proof of downstream follow-up, outcomes, broad generalization, or scale.

sources.title: Pivotal trial of an autonomous AI-based diagnostic system for detection of diabetic retinopathy in primary care offices
sources.geographyPopulation: 900 people with diabetes and no history of diabetic retinopathy at 10 US primary-care sites
sources.deadline: Primary-care encounter workflow; not a universal latency benchmark
sources.intendedUse: Detect more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edema against a reading-center reference
sources.denominatorUnit: Enrolled participants and analyzable diagnostic encounters
sources.role: Prospective validation for bounded autonomous diagnosis
sources.interpretation: Supports demonstrated diagnostic performance under trial conditions.
sources.caveat: Enrichment, eligibility, image acquisition, reference standard, and trial workflow limit generalization.

sources.institution: npj Digital Medicine / Johns Hopkins Medicine
sources.title: Autonomous artificial intelligence for diabetic eye disease increases access and health equity in underserved populations
sources.geographyPopulation: More than 17,000 adults with diabetes in a largely metropolitan US health system
sources.deadline: Primary-care encounter and annual screening workflow
sources.intendedUse: Autonomous diabetic eye disease testing in selected primary-care sites
sources.denominatorUnit: Annual testing adherence among health-system patients with diabetes
sources.role: Documents operational deployment and access association
sources.interpretation: AI-switched sites had a larger adjusted increase in annual testing adherence than non-AI sites.
sources.caveat: Retrospective, largely metropolitan comparison cannot by itself establish causality, completed referral, outcomes, or broad scale.

sources.title: MLPerf Inference v6.0 benchmark results
sources.geographyPopulation: Submitted benchmark systems; no human population
sources.deadline: The interactive DeepSeek-R1 scenario constrains response latency under the round's workload and compliance rules
sources.intendedUse: Compare inference systems under defined workload, quality, latency, and compliance rules
sources.denominatorUnit: Benchmark queries and generated tokens on specified reasoning workloads, model, scenario, hardware, and software
sources.role: Establishes measurable interactive-generation latency with quality constraints
sources.interpretation: Interactive response cadence is a testable system property.
sources.caveat: Benchmark compliance does not establish factuality, field reliability, application completion, or service-wide performance.

sources.institution: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
sources.title: StreamDiffusion: A Pipeline-level Solution for Real-Time Interactive Generation
sources.geographyPopulation: Research models, inputs, and tested GPU hardware; no population estimate
sources.period: Experiments reported in peer-reviewed ICCV 2025 paper
sources.deadline: Interactive frame or image cadence on specified pipeline and hardware
sources.intendedUse: Continuous diffusion generation from changing inputs
sources.denominatorUnit: Generated frames or images per unit time under reported models, resolutions, and hardware
sources.interpretation: Pipeline changes can move diffusion generation into interactive timing on tested systems.
sources.caveat: Hardware-specific research performance does not prove operational reliability, safe content, rights clearance, or scale.

sources.title: MLPerf Inference benchmark definitions
sources.date: v5.0 definitions retained as a pinned benchmark case; current suite reviewed September 1, 2026
sources.geographyPopulation: ImageNet-2012 and OpenImages benchmark validation data; submitted systems
sources.period: Pinned v5.0 benchmark definitions reviewed September 1, 2026; v6.0 changed the edge object-detection workload
sources.deadline: Scenario- and model-specific constraints; ResNet50 server latency constraint listed as 15 ms
sources.intendedUse: Measure image classification and object-detection inference while meeting quality targets
sources.denominatorUnit: Fixed benchmark queries, validation samples, accuracy targets, load scenarios, hardware, and software
sources.role: Separates benchmark latency from accuracy for bounded vision tasks
sources.interpretation: A system can be tested against both timing and quality requirements.
sources.caveat: Fixed benchmark data do not establish open-world reliability, sensor robustness, downstream decision quality, or safety.

sources.title: Pick planning strategies for large-scale package manipulation
sources.geographyPopulation: Amazon Robotics Robin production fleet and handled packages; sites not enumerated
sources.period: Cumulative and daily volume reported in 2023 extended abstract
sources.deadline: Production induction cadence; no per-pick latency distribution reported
sources.intendedUse: Pick and singulate packages from unstructured piles using learned pick-success estimates
sources.denominatorUnit: Vendor reports up to 6 million packages per day and more than 2 billion cumulative manipulations
sources.role: Establishes bounded production deployment and aggregate scale
sources.interpretation: Learned pick planning operated at material volume in one warehouse task.
sources.caveat: Vendor-authored aggregate claims lack independent site, reliability, intervention, economics, and worker-outcome denominators.

sources.title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure
sources.geographyPopulation: Global employment mapped through occupational tasks and harmonized microdata
sources.intendedUse: Estimate occupational task exposure to generative AI
sources.denominatorUnit: Employment shares and task-level exposure gradients; not observed job loss
sources.interpretation: Because occupations combine tasks requiring human input, job transformation is more likely than direct one-to-one replacement in the index.
sources.caveat: Exposure is modeled capability overlap, not adoption, reliable full-loop automation, displacement, or forecast timing.

sources.institution: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.date: January 26, 2023; current resource page reviewed September 1, 2026
sources.geographyPopulation: Cross-sector organizations, AI actors, affected individuals, groups, communities, and society
sources.deadline: Calls for continuous, timely lifecycle risk management rather than one universal system deadline
sources.intendedUse: Map, measure, govern, and manage AI risks for specific tasks and contexts
sources.denominatorUnit: Qualitative risk-management outcomes and documented evaluations; not a maturity score
sources.role: Supports task scope, human oversight, contingency, impact, and monitoring structure
sources.interpretation: Capabilities, limits, intended use, oversight, impacts, and emergent risks must be documented across a system lifecycle.
sources.caveat: Voluntary framework guidance does not certify any case, maturity flag, reliability level, or legal compliance.
